To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1) the folding of IFN- γ in the ER is regulated by a multi-chaperon complex and 2) calreticulin is the major chaperon interacting with IFN - γ during heat shock.
the ER multi-chaperone complexes are involved in the folding regulation of cytokines in vivo and in vitro.
the cytokine IFN-γ folds in association with a multi-chaperon complex and is maintained in a folding competent form by calretiulin during heat shock.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the cellular mechanisms regulating cytokine folding and the characterization of their role in cytokine homeostasis.

the identification of chaperone complexes involved in the folding and secretion of cytokines in mammalian cells, and the role of these chaperones in maintaining cytokine folding competence under conditions associated with fever.
the quality control mechanisms regulating the folding and trafficking of secreted proteins in the endoplamic reticulum.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
IFN-γ folds in the ER in association with a multi-chaperon complex, and that the folding process is regulated by ATP.
the ER folding of cytokines is regulated by a multi-chaperon complex, which includes GRP94, ERp72 and CaBP1/PDI, and that the folding of cytokine dimers in vivo is protected by calreticulen.
IFN-γ folding in the endoplasic reticulum is regulated by a multi-chaperon complex.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ER quality control machinery is more versatile than previously thought, and is able to cope with a variety of protein folding situations.
the folding of IFNγ is controlled by a multi-chaperon complex that is regulated co-ordinatly by ATP, and that calreticulin is a major chaperone for IFNγ during heat-shock.
the folding of the cytokines IFN-γ (and possibly IL-10) is regulated in a co-ordinated fashion by a multi-chaperon complex in the ER and by calreticuline in the cytosol.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the folding of IFN- γ is a complex process involving multiple chaperones, and that this folding is regulated by both ATP and the redox environment in the ER.

the ER chaperone machinery can be regulated by ATP, and that the chaperone complex is likely to be involved in the folding and quality control of a wide spectrum of ER proteins, from simple cytokines to large, multi-subunit complexes.
the folding of the cytokines interferon-γ and interleukin- 10 is regulated by a multi-chaperon complex, and calreticulin is the major chaperon involved in the thermo-protection of these cytokines.
